thread:
incident-bot: paging @jordan (primary on-call) — elevated error rate on request signing: Cloud KMS API timeouts observed across multiple regions. Startup jobs failing with signing errors. Auto-pager triggered.

jordan (oncall): ack. seeing alerts in prod (signing_error_rate > 5%). which KMS provider?

samir (eng-runtime): looks like both AWS KMS and GCP KMS calls are returning 503/504 intermittently. stack traces from failed startup: 
```
2026-03-15T02:02:47Z error signing request: kms: ListKeys call timed out after 10s
2026-03-15T02:02:47Z warn startup failed: could not sign service token: context deadline exceeded
github.com/redwood/inference/internal/signing.(*KMSClient).Sign
```

maria (sre): dashboards show spike at 02:01 UTC — KMS client retries are amplifying load. downstream request latencies spiking, some frontends falling into 502s. adding graph links: https://grafana/redwood/graphs?panel=signing_errors (posted)

emily (support): Support queue getting inbound messages: two customers on Dedicated reported jobs stuck in INIT and errors include "unable to fetch key". sending customer-safe status note now.

jordan (oncall): immediate mitigation proposals — (1) short-circuit non-essential background jobs that do on-start KMS key discovery, (2) flip runtime to use local cached keys for existing VM pools, (3) temporarily reduce KMS retry multiplier and increase backoff to avoid thundering herd. any objections?

samir (eng-runtime): no objections. we have a runtime flag `REDWOOD_KMS_CACHE_MODE=readonly` that will let existing cached keys be used for signing for 30m. can patch deploy to control planes and Dedicated agents. patch contains: 
```
# infra patch (safe rollback)
- set REDWOOD_KMS_CACHE_MODE=readonly
- set KMS_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS=2000
- disable background key-discovery cron
```

maria (sre): will apply change to Hosted control plane canaries first (us-west2). ops runbook step: mark change as emergency, set deploy to 2-min window. I'll coordinate.

nate (ops-lead): open support ticket with cloud vendors in parallel — I'm escalating to AWS support for account-level API degradation and to GCP. aws-status-bot, do we have public incident?

aws-status-bot: AWS KMS: We are investigating increased error rates for the kms.amazonaws.com endpoint in multiple regions. (link to AWS status)

jordan (oncall): thanks. maria, samir — execute mitigation steps and post rollout status here. emily, prep customer comms: include impact, affected services, and ETA for the mitigation. I'll keep paged until stable.

samir (eng-runtime): deploying cache-mode to canary in us-west2 now. commands: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/control-plane-runner REDWOOD_KMS_CACHE_MODE=readonly -n redwood-control
kubectl set env deployment/agent REDWOOD_KMS_CACHE_MODE=readonly -n redwood-agent
```

(2m later) samir (eng-runtime): canary looks stable, signing error rate dropped from 6.2% to 0.4% on canary hosts. rolling to remaining control-plane nodes.

maria (sre): rolling to Dedicated pools paused at 30% due to degraded host metrics on one cluster — investigating.

emily (support): customer note posted: "We're seeing degraded signing calls to cloud KMS which causes job startup failures in a subset of environments. We're deploying a temporary cache-mode to reduce impact. More updates in 15m." (link to status tile) :loudspeaker:

nate (ops-lead): AWS/ GCP cases opened: AWS case #12345678, GCP case #87654321. vendor response ETA 20m.

jordan (oncall): update on-call handoff: I'm handing primary to @samir for the next 30 minutes to complete the rollout, then @maria will own stabilization and postmortem. continuing to monitor.

samir (eng-runtime): rollout complete to all control plane and agents. global signing error rate down to 0.3%. continuing to watch for retries and edge cases.

maria (sre): observing slower consumer queues and some catch-up traffic causing CPU spikes — scaling agent pools by +20% to absorb backlog.

emily (support): two enterprise customers (Customer A, Customer B) hit transient job failures — both informed. Customer A asked for ETA on full resolution; we replied ~2h pending vendor root cause.

aws-status-bot: AWS update: "API rate-limiting and elevated latencies in kms.amazonaws.com subsystems affecting some customers. Working on mitigation."

jordan (oncall): Per impact assessment: ~1.7% of global sign attempts errored during peak — produced ~0.6% customer-visible job failures (mostly Dedicated and Private). mitigations reduced visible failures to <0.1%. posting incident severity as Sev2 for now.

samir (eng-runtime): follow-ups: (a) add exponential jitter to KMS client retries, (b) add longer-lived local key cache option for Dedicated, (c) add better outage-mode telemetry to differentiate provider vs local issues. filing tickets.

maria (sre): I'll start timeline and request logs for postmortem. please drop any console commands or unusual logs in this thread.

nate (ops-lead): closing loop with vendor once we get root cause. good job team. handing final on-call to @maria for post-incident tasks.

jordan (oncall): thanks all — monitoring until we see two hours stable. incident-bot: set incident status to "stabilized" and create incident channel for postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident marked stabilized by @jordan. Incident channel #incident-1871234567 created for postmortem drafting.
